message.content: We don’t have a definitive “largest planet” in the entire universe—our knowledge is limited to what we’ve observed so far. Among the planets we’ve discovered outside our Solar System (exoplanets), the biggest ones are often classified as “super‑Jupiters.” One of the most massive and inflated exoplanets we know of is **HD 100546 b**, which has an estimated radius of about 10–12 times that of Jupiter and a mass roughly 20–30 times Jupiter’s mass. However, there may well be larger planets out there that we haven’t detected yet, especially if they’re farther away or orbiting dimmer stars. In short, the largest planet we currently know of is a super‑Jupiter like HD 100546 b, but the true maximum size remains unknown.
